name: Solenne Neuralcrest Lattice Crown
description:
An architectural neural-port fascinator rebuilt as a full crown piece — Solenne's answer to criticism that their earlier port cover was too subtle for Spire event wear. The Lattice Crown is constructed from hand-bent gold-titanium wire in an open lattice structure that frames the skull without touching it, anchored by a slim internal headband of ivory synth-suede. Micro-filament bioluminescent threads are woven through the lattice, pulsing in slow waves synchronized to the wearer's BCI heartbeat data.

Designed to display — not conceal — cranial chrome and neural port hardware as deliberate aesthetic centerpieces. Custom-fitted per client.
functionality: BCI-synchronized bioluminescent pulse display; structural lattice keeps all elements elevated from scalp to prevent interference with port hardware; custom-fitted to client's specific cranial chrome layout; headband includes inductive charge pad for continuous filament power.
what_it_says: Your augmentation is not something you hide — it is the most expensive thing in the room.
story_hooks: A Lattice Crown commissioned for a Helix Corp board director was intercepted in transit — the BCI sync module contains a passive data-skimming exploit.
One crown's bioluminescent pulse pattern has been quietly encoding the wearer's real-time emotional state, readable by anyone with the right decryption key.
A Solenne atelier artisan is selling unauthorized duplicate fittings — meaning someone has a precise map of a Spire client's cranial hardware layout.
